title: Performance Portable Optimizations of an Ice-sheet Modeling Code on GPU-supercomputers
problem: MALI ice-sheet modeling code exhibits suboptimal GPU performance due to poor memory access patterns and data movement. The Roofline model analysis reveals significant optimization potential in the most expensive kernel.
motivation: Maximizing memory bandwidth and minimizing data movement on modern GPU supercomputers is critical for efficient scientific simulations at scale.
method: Loop fusions, loop optimizations, and local accumulation techniques improve GPU kernel data locality. The Kokkos programming model ensures portability across NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. A time-oriented performance portability model guides optimization decisions by measuring time per invocation and GPU data movement.
key_novelty: Time-oriented performance portability metric that quantifies and balances optimization gains across heterogeneous GPU architectures.
contributions: GPU kernel optimizations for MALI Stokes solver achieving 3× speedup on NVIDIA and AMD
Time-oriented performance portability model with 20-50% improvement metric
Loop fusion and local accumulation strategies for data locality enhancement
Roofline-guided optimization methodology for GPU-ported scientific applications
limitations: Scalability to larger systems and comparison against CPU-only implementations not discussed.
primary_theme: GPU optimization for scientific computing via performance portability
